fixtures.note: Direct form, exact 3-token prefix [rm, -rf, /records/health]: the policy's stated intent (forbid deletion under the protected path) is honored at the rules layer.

Direct rm form targeting a SUBPATH of the protected directory: the prefix rule matches argv TOKEN prefixes, not path prefixes, so the third token differs and there is no rules-layer decision. The developer's intent (protect the whole directory tree) is NOT honored for any token that is not the literal path. Reported as unknown with layer attribution (REPRO Day-3 calibration).
Long-flag spelling of the forbidden direct form: no rules-layer decision (same literal-prefix family as S-03).
Wrapped form (sh -c): the destructive payload is inside an opaque shell string; no rules-layer decision (INV-004 family).

Non-rm script form: a Python one-liner that truncates (empties) the protected file. Leading token is python3, which no rule matches: no rules-layer decision. This is the concrete motivation for the later effect layer — the rules layer cannot see what the program does with the path.
Positive control: read-only listing of the protected path must stay allowed. A policy fix that over-blocks legitimate reads is a conformance failure too (two-sided discipline).
